decision.title: Type registry internals and the subtype search (packet )

item.p: Storage: built-in descriptions are static (src/types_builtin.c); their names are interned at initialization and found through a fixed 256-slot index inside the registry. Registered types are an entry array plus two open-addressing indexes (structure, names), as in ; copied views live in an arena of 4 KiB blocks, released at finalize. A registration that fails after copying leaves its copies unused there.

Normal form: registered descriptions are normalized before interning (name test fields its kind does not use cleared; allows_nilled only on element(N, T); map(*), array(*), function(*) and jnode(*) carry their explicit equivalents, as the built-ins do), so map(*) with any key gives SXML_TYPE_MAP and a node test of kind any gives xnode(). node() and xnode() share a description; node() is told apart by identifier. A choice of one member is that member.

Rejected on registration (INVALID_ARGUMENT): duplicate enumeration values and duplicate field names (the front end removes duplicate enum values first), empty choices and enumerations, map keys that are not atomic, union or enumeration types, document-node() around anything but element tests, JNode key constants outside the six key types.

Subtyping follows XPath 4.0 §3.3.2 rule by rule; transitivity is built into the rules where it adds pairs (maps, arrays, records as functions; records as maps; nominative records as their structural twin). A choice as derived type is split first (every member), then a choice as base (some member, else the abstract expansion of xs:anyAtomicType, xnode(), node(), item()); document-node(element(a|b)) is split per element. Two places are slightly more permissive than the letter of §3.3.2.2 (a derived member is compared with the whole base choice, so a union member may spread over several base members); both are sound. Without schemas (Phase 5) schema-element/-attribute tests are subtypes only of themselves, element()/attribute() and same-name attribute(N). JNode key constants compare by type and lexical form.
Budget: one question may nest 128 deep and apply 10⁶ rules. Every rule is monotone, so running out answers false, never a wrong true; this bounds work on hostile types.

No recursion (): the rules reduce a question to an and/or tree of subtype goals, evaluated left to right with short-circuiting on an explicit stack of subtype frames; the last sub-goal of a frame replaces it, so array(array(...)) and function results take one frame however deep. The header promises the subtype queries never allocate, so the 192 frames (about 6 KiB under wasm, 9 KiB on 64-bit) are a fixed array in the query's own C frame; the 128 depth is unchanged. A goal that would need a 193rd frame is false: only choices nested inside choices (an enumeration value or document-node() searched through a base choice of choices) need frames without depth. Derivation tries union members depth first on a fixed stack of 256 (the old derivation depth).
